_what: THE ONE PLACE A CERTIFICATION-SPECIFIC WRITER INSTRUCTION LIVES for AIMS-IA. Read by gen-grounded-items, which appends `cert_notes` to the system prompt for every task and any `notes.<task>` entry to that task's prompt only. A ruling that belongs to one certification does not go in the shared system prompt (PROMPT-126 s2).
_cert_notes_what: Appended to the SYSTEM prompt on every AIMS-IA task. Carried over from ISMS-IA at PROMPT-136 s2 because it is a lesson about item quality, not about ISO/IEC 27001: the three ISMS-IA rejections it records were all answerable by elimination, which is a defect any certification can have.
cert_notes:
EVERY DISTRACTOR MUST BE A MISTAKE SOMEONE COULD ACTUALLY MAKE (ruled PROMPT-127 s4, carried to AIMS-IA by PROMPT-136 s2):

- Every distractor must be a mistake a working auditor or AI management system manager could
  plausibly make. No option may be rejectable on common sense alone. Prefer a short scenario that
  requires APPLYING the clause over asking for the definition.
- This is why three of thirteen items were rejected on the first ISMS-IA round: a "visit calendar
  the certification body sets", "headcount", "the cheapest controls available", and a strawman
  naming a certification body's major nonconformities. Each was answerable by elimination without
  knowing the clause, which makes the item measure nothing.

NO ISO/IEC 27000-FAMILY DEFINITIONS AS THE KEY. This is an ISO/IEC 42001 certification. The 27000
family -- 27000, 27001, 27002 -- is SUPPORT ONLY here: it may inform a distractor's reason and
never carries the key. A requirements key rests on an ISO/IEC 42001 `shall` passage, Annex A
controls included; an audit-practice key rests on ISO 19011. ISO/IEC 42001 ANNEX B is
implementation guidance for an Annex A control and is support only too: key on the control.

notes._what: Per-task instructions, appended to THAT task's prompt only. Empty at creation: a task note is a ruling about one task and is added when the director makes one. ISMS-IA's notes were all written after a round was read, never before.

4.11.instruction: The key anchors on the 4.1 climate sentence or the 4.2 climate note. Distractor support comes from 4.3 or 6.1.1. Note that 4.2's climate line is a NOTE, so a key on it states what interested parties CAN have, never what the organization MUST do.

1.2.instruction: Don't key on risk-based sampling being reconciled with evidence-based conclusions. That point is already tested. Don't key on weighting audit time or effort toward high-risk or poorly performing areas. That point is already tested.

2.3.instruction: Don't key on the technical expert's role relative to the auditors. That point is already tested.

2.5.instruction: Don't key on statutory findings being called non-compliance. That point is already tested. Don't key on statutory findings being called non-compliance, or on the organization's own procedures counting as audit criteria. That point is already tested.

3.8.instruction: Don't key on recording an unresolved disagreement. That point is tested twice already.

4.5.instruction: The key must anchor on ISO/IEC 42001 6.1.3 or 8.3. These points are ALREADY TESTED on those two passages and must not be the key: that a documented justification for excluding a control is acceptable when it traces to that system's risk assessment; that a control neither documented nor communicated is unsupported; that 6.1.3 asks for guidance to be taken into account and the organization may implement a control in its own way; that a changed treatment option needs evidence of review and revalidation with the plan updated; that implementation without verification of effectiveness leaves a declaration unsupported; and that a register entry with an owner is not a risk treatment process. Key on something else in those two clauses.
